facts.statement: Westralichthys is an extinct genus containing only one species of dunkleosteoid fish.
facts.quote: Westralichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of dunkleosteoid

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single fossil skull identified as WAM 86.9.664.
facts.quote: Known from only a single skull, WAM 86.9.664

facts.statement: Scientists estimate the animal reached a length of 3 meters.
facts.quote: It is estimated to be 3 m long

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Virgin Hills Formation of Western Australia dating to the Middle Famennian stage of the Late Devonian.
facts.quote: from the Late Devonian, Middle Famennian stage from the Virgin Hills Formation, Western Australia

facts.statement: The name Westralichthys combines 'Western' for the Australian state and 'ichthys' for fish.
facts.quote: The name refers to the state of Western Australia, with ichthys meaning fish

facts.statement: The genus was first described by Long in 1987.
Westralichthys belongs to the superfamily Dunkleosteoidea and is related to the giant Dunkleosteus.
facts.quote: Westralichthys belongs to the superfamily Dunkleosteoidea, related to the giant Dunkleosteus

facts.statement: The animal is classified within the family Dinichthyidae.
Westralichthys is a member of the class Placodermi.
The species lived between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (372.15 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of this genus in the Paleobiology Database.
